title: Why Texas Runs Its Own Power Grid #shorts
summary: ERCOT, Texas's own interconnection, serves more than 27 million customers, about 90% of the state's electric load.
sources: ERCOT serves more than 27 million Texas customers, about 90 percent of the state's electric load (ERCOT, About ERCOT): https://www.ercot.com/about

The lower 48 run on interconnections (Eastern, Western, Texas/ERCOT) that operate at a synchronized frequency averaging 60 Hz (US DOE Office of Electricity, Learn more about interconnections): https://www.energy.gov/oe/learn-more-about-interconnections

scenes.narration: Texas has its own power grid.
It's called ERCOT, and it serves about {90%|ninety percent} of the state's electric load.
That's more than {27 million|twenty-seven million} customers.
The rest of the lower {48|forty-eight} mostly share two big grids: East and West.
Everyone else shares. Texas has its own grid.
